*Fix* (`gov/exchange_ledger.py`, spec `evals/f165_f166_f170_ledger_robustness_spec.md` via to-spec):
- F165: `_validated_window_sec()` returns `(ok, value, raw)`; a *parsed* non-positive `GOV_EXCHANGE_WINDOW_SEC` denies window-dependent (default-posture) cross-run reads with an audited `exchange_read_denied` record naming the bad value + `ExchangeAccessDenied`. Posture: **deny**, not clamp (clamping silently rewrites explicit broken intent) and not `ValueError` (the seam speaks `ExchangeAccessDenied`). Validation sits only on the default-posture path — own-run reads (early return above), allowlisted and strict-posture reads (never consult the window) are unaffected, so a broken window cannot brick own-run reads. Unparseable values keep the documented default 900 (status quo the audit confirmed safe). Threshold knobs analyzed, no change: non-positive `MAX_RUNS`/`MAX_SINGLE_READ` already over-deny (fail-closed), non-numeric fall back to defaults.
- F166: records carry `mono` (`time.monotonic()` at record time) and `boot` (boot-epoch id — `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id` read once per process and cached, conservative per-process fallback on non-Linux). `_record_in_window`: same-epoch records gate on monotonic only (immune to clock jumps either direction); cross-epoch and legacy (field-less) records keep counting by wall-clock `ts` — the fail-closed direction, so a restart does not launder the budget. `ts` remains the human-readable audit timestamp. **Considered deviation from the filing's one-liner** ("wall-clock must not gate the tripwire"): cross-epoch records *are* wall-gated, fail-closed-counting — authorized by the lane brief and spec'd, because the alternative (cross-epoch ⇒ expired) would be a restart-launders-budget fail-open strictly worse than the finding.
- F170: `_read_window_full` scans at most a tail byte budget (`_tail_budget`, default `max(2MB, window_sec·512)`, env `GOV_EXCHANGE_LEDGER_TAIL_BYTES`); truncated scan with no trip denies fail-closed ("cannot prove the allow case"), a trip from partial data still denies with the tripwire reason. Append-time compaction past `_compact_threshold` (default `max(1MB, window_sec·256)`, env `GOV_EXCHANGE_LEDGER_COMPACT_BYTES`) rewrites the file keeping only window-relevant records — atomic temp-file + `os.replace` with temp fsync + directory fsync (crash leaves old *or* new complete file, never a truncation), stale-fd identity check with ≤3 retries against the replace-vs-concurrent-appender race, module-level `_APPEND_LOCK` because fcntl does not exclude threads. Any compaction failure degrades to `ExchangeAccessDenied`, never to unbounded growth. Size knobs garbage/non-positive ⇒ default (knobs can only move toward deny, never allow).

**F69 timing-flake hardening lane (2026-09-26)** — F69 stays LOW/CLOSED; this is test-flake hardening, not a finding re-open. No commit/push (active tree only). Workflow: `diagnosing-bugs` (red-first) -> `tdd` -> two-axis `code-review` (Standards + Spec, independent subagents).

*Failure shape.* `tests/test_hardening_r16.py::TestF69WarmTipBounded::test_warm_tip_refused_sweep_bounded_at_20k` flaked under concurrent-lane CPU load. Deterministic repro on the pre-fix tree: two CPU burners + the test x3 -> 3/3 FAILED at 301/328/391ms wall vs the 150ms bound.

*Root cause.* `time.perf_counter()` measures scheduler descheduling as if it were sweep cost — under saturation wall/CPU ratios ran 2.7-6.6x while sweep CPU stayed flat. Falsified: full-`verify_chain()` fallback and executor construction inside the timer. F69's property is bounded CPU work, so the test now asserts the bound on `time.process_time()` (the per-sweep tip-write fsync is O(1), not the amplifier). Second root cause the diagnosis surfaced: `_read_tip_cache`'s F72 replay-freshness scan JSON-parsed the ENTIRE checkpoint sidecar on every warm sweep (~60-80ms of ~95ms at 20k) — an O(sidecar) term eating most of the bound. It now scans from the tip's `pin_off` (sidecar offset measured before the tip's own pin appends): O(new bytes). A naive `cp_size`-suffix first attempt was rejected by Spec review as unsound under concurrent tip writers (a newer pin interleaved between the pin append and the cp_size measurement would be missed -> silent stale accept); the `pin_off` design fixes that race (red-capable regression test). `pin_off` is MAC-covered; tips without it fail closed and reseed via full re-verify.

*Red-first evidence.* New `TestF69PinScanIncremental` (2 tests): (1) scan-size spy — red pre-fix (414KB scanned of a 414KB sidecar), green post-fix; (2) racy-newer-pin interleave — red against the naive `cp_size` scan, green with `pin_off`. Process incident (honest): mid-lane, same-second `sed` edits left a stale `__pycache__/log.cpython-312.pyc` that Python treated as fresh (mtime granularity), producing phantom "pass in isolation, fail in suite" results; cleared all `__pycache__` and re-verified everything with fresh bytecode.

*Gates (venv `~/workspace/.gov-venv`).* Focused flake test: 5/5 green under full 2-CPU saturation (pre-fix: 3/3 red under identical load); quiet green. `test_hardening_r16` + `test_hardening_r23` + `test_log_merkle`: 42/42 green normally and under `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`. Bound still discriminates pre-R16 behavior (no-tip full verify: 759-773ms CPU vs the 150ms bound). Warm-sweep CPU: ~16ms post-fix (was ~95ms), 9x headroom. F72 replay + F70 manifest suites green both envs.

*Two-axis review* (`evals/f69_timing_flake_two_axis_review.md`): Standards — 3 findings fixed in-lane (test class past `__main__` guard, split validation, stray local import; trimmed comment). Spec — 1 soundness finding fixed via `pin_off` (the naive-scan race), re-review CONDITIONAL PASS: honest residual recorded (a writer racing an interleaved pin append *before* the measurement can leave a genuine higher-gen pin before `pin_off`; a stale-but-genuine tip may then be accepted — safe, not a replay hole: tip is MAC-authentic and vouches a verified prefix, the incremental walk re-verifies the tail with full per-entry checks, and the new window supersedes the old so the change only adds rejections). Residual carried in `evals/FINDINGS.md` maintenance note under F69.

## 2026-09-27 — attenu-guard adaptation lane (offline evidence bundle exporter + standalone verifier)

**Scope:** Adapt attenu-io/attenu-guard's offline evidence-bundle design (Apache-2.0, credited in-module) — self-contained bundle + standalone verifier, JCS-style canonicalization, signed anchor, integrity/monotonicity/containment checks, explicit redaction report, zero runtime dependencies — to our audit log + anchor receipt. No attenu-guard code copied (not available offline); design adapted, not cloned.

**New files (no existing files modified):**
- `gov/offline_bundle.py` — `export_offline_bundle()`: verifies the source HMAC chain, selects a seq window, requires per-entry Ed25519 signatures under a single key (now VALIDATED at export, see hardening below), applies field redaction (never chain bookkeeping), builds an unkeyed export chain over exactly the shipped bytes, anchors the tip+window+redaction-digest via the anchor adapter, writes `VERSION`/`ledger.jsonl`/`manifest.json`/`anchor_receipt.json`/`REDACTION_REPORT.txt`/`BUNDLE_DIGEST.sha256`.
- `tools/offline-verify` — standalone verifier (stdlib only: argparse/hashlib/json/os/sys; zero repo imports; runs with PYTHONPATH scrubbed). Checks: T1 transport digest, V0 version, I2/I3 monotonicity+containment, I1 export-chain integrity, A1 anchor authenticity (two-level statement hash + log_id + Ed25519 SET signature + Merkle inclusion), R1 redaction honesty (sig-or-listed). Exit 0=VERIFIED (both pins), 2=SELF_CONSISTENT (unpinned), 1=FAILED. Prints the honesty footer on every run.
- `tests/test_offline_bundle.py` — 10 unit tests (export shape, fail-closed refusals, redaction listing, window subslice).
- `evals/offline_bundle_adversarial.py` — 8-probe break-first battery (5 attacks + 3 controls), verifier executed as a scrubbed subprocess.

**Red-first cycle (honest):** probes written before the verifier. v0 (chain/monotonicity/containment/statement-match only) → b4_forged_receipt BREAK (garbage log_sig accepted — the anchor signature wasn't checked) and the honest-bundle controls broke on a v0 statement-hash bug (single-level vs the adapter's two-level `bundle_statement`+`_statement_hash`). Fixed the statement computation, added A1 (SET signature + Merkle inclusion + log_id binding) and R1 (per-entry sig-or-listed). v1: **8/8 HELD**.

**Exporter hardening during development:** the exporter initially checked signature *presence* but did not *verify* per-entry Ed25519 signatures at export time (a corrupted-signature log would export a doomed bundle; the verifier's R1 would still reject it — fail-closed at verification, but not at export). Added export-time validation under the required `entry_signer_pubkey` (fail-closed `OfflineBundleError`); unit test `test_refuses_invalid_entry_signature` pins it. `entry_signer_pubkey` is now REQUIRED so every bundle is self-contained.

**Key design points:** the source HMAC chain can't be recomputed offline (operator key never leaves the operator), so the export chain is deliberately unkeyed SHA-256 — its security comes from the ANCHOR (Ed25519-signed receipt committing to tip+window+redaction-digest), not key secrecy (battery b1/b4 pin this). Per-entry Ed25519 signatures give offline content authentication; redacted entries drop their (now-unverifiable) signatures and MUST be listed — a silently-redacted entry has neither and is rejected (b5). Unpinned verification is honestly labeled SELF_CONSISTENT, never authorship.

**Evidence:** `tests/test_offline_bundle.py` 10/10 OK; `evals/offline_bundle_adversarial.py` 8/8 HELD (b1 full rewrite, b2 tamper, b3 drop, b4 forged receipt, b5 redaction lie, c1 pinned VERIFIED, c2 unpinned SELF_CONSISTENT, c3 legit redaction).

**Two-axis review:** Standards PASS (module-level GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE=staging, standalone verified under scrubbed env, deterministic, $0, fail-closed, Apache-2.0 attribution, no existing files touched); Spec PASS (exporter + standalone verifier + I1/I2/I3 from bundle alone + explicit redaction report + deterministic tests + this entry + review; no push).

**Findings:** none filed. The export-time signature hardening was a development-time catch (verifier was always fail-closed; fixed before commit) — does not meet the finding bar. Next free: **F178**. Open findings: F176, F177 (unchanged).

## 2026-09-27 — Cedar Request/Decision+Diagnostics contract adaptation (no push)

**Scope:** Adapt two interface ideas from cedar-policy/cedar (Apache-2.0, © Cedar Contributors; main branch, README + `cedar-policy/src/api.rs` fetched 2026-09-27; exact upstream commit SHA not captured — provenance recorded at branch/date level per the intent-slice precedent; NO upstream code copied, interface adapted): (1) a typed `Request → Decision+Diagnostics` authorization contract — every authorization takes a well-typed Request and returns a Decision with structured Diagnostics explaining WHY (which policies matched, which forbid-clauses fired); (2) forbid-overrides-permit semantics — explicit deny wins over permits regardless of declaration order. Deliberate delta from Cedar: the third verdict `require_approval` is preserved first-class (deny > require_approval > allow), not collapsed to binary allow/deny — documented in-module.

**New files:**
- `gov/decision_contract.py` — frozen dataclasses: `Request` (principal, action, resource, role, args, context; validated in `__post_init__`, `ContractError` on malformed input), `Decision` (effect, allowed with `__post_init__` invariant `allowed == (effect == "allow")`, reason, policy_id, flag, diagnostics, request), `Diagnostics` (deciding_rule, forbid_hits, approval_hits, permit_hits, shadowed hits, full trace, flat policy-id set), `RuleHit` (rule id, effect, reason, flag, declaration index, decider flag), `TraceEntry` (effect, rule_id, matched). `Request.from_action()` is the legacy-bridge constructor (principal falls through `agent_id → agent → "unknown"`; `tool=None` retained for platform-egress evaluations; resource derived best-effort for diagnostics only). `Decision.to_policy_decision()` preserves legacy `PolicyDecision` fields and `matched_rules` semantics exactly. Stdlib only (dataclasses/typing).
- `evals/cedar_contract_probes.py` — 12-probe break-first battery (module-level `GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE=staging`; standalone verified under `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`): p1 permit-declared-first, p2 forbid-declared-first, p3 multiple matching forbids all named, p4 narrow forbid vs broad permit, p5 non-matching forbid no false deny, p6 implicit-deny diagnostics, p7 deny > approval > allow under hostile ordering, p8 diagnostics misattribution resistance (decider flag + shadowed hits), p9 shadowed permit stays visible, p10 malformed/untyped Requests fail loudly, p11 decide() vs legacy evaluate() differential (21 engine/case pairs), p12 trace structurally shows deny pass before permit pass. Result: **12/12 HELD, 0 BREAK, 0 ERROR** (two initial BREAKs were probe defects — wrong trace-entry count, wrong counter key — not product defects).

**Refactor (existing files):** `gov/policy.py` — added `PolicyEngine.decide(request)` (typed entry; evaluates deny → require_approval → allow passes, collects ALL matches + full trace, first match within the winning pass decides; no match = fail-closed `default_deny`); `evaluate(action, context)` now delegates (`decide(Request.from_action(action, context)).to_policy_decision()`). Transparency hardening during review: `from_action` is a PURE PROJECTION of the action dict — nothing promoted from context (role/agent taken from the action only) — and `decide()` uses the caller's context unmodified (no role/agent injection into the match context), so the action reaching `_matches` is identical to the original on every key `_matches` reads (tool, role, agent_id, args). Extra action keys (`identity`, bare `agent`) are dropped by the round-trip; verified inert (no `_matches` key reads them; no in-tree caller relies on them for matching).

**Latency (honest):** measured 2026-09-27, 2,000 calls against the 27-rule default policy: old early-exit `evaluate` = 16.8 µs/call; new `decide` (full trace) = 78.8 µs/call; delta = **+62 µs/call (4.7×)**. The cost is structural and by design: the contract evaluates all rules and builds trace/dataclass diagnostics instead of short-circuiting at the deciding rule. Absolute cost is ~0.06 ms per authorization — immaterial against a tool call (ms-scale: process spawn, HMAC-chained audit write) — but the relative 4.7× is real and reported, not hidden. Review decision: keep always-on full diagnostics; the evidence value (every fired forbid/permit named, full trace) justifies the absolute cost. (A review subagent independently measured ~127.5 µs/op on the same shape — same order, methodology/load dependent.)

**Two-axis review:** Standards **PASS WITH NOTES** (6 minor findings, all fixed: dead `field` import; function-level import hoisted to module level; duplicated rule-id fallback computed once; `_mark` rewritten with `dataclasses.replace`; duplicated p7 probe computation removed; lazy-import cycle comment added). Spec: (a) MET · (b) MET (transparency proven by construction + suite) · (c) MET · (d) MET with caveat · (e) recorded here (reviewer couldn't find the measurement — it now lives in this entry). Spec residuals, all documented: p11 differential is shim-consistency, not pre-contract equivalence (real proof is the 3790-test suite); `to_action()` drops non-matching action keys (verified inert); diagnostics not yet wired into audit-log/refusal surfaces — `evaluate()` is the only in-tree `decide()` caller, so the "why" is currently battery-available, not operator-visible (follow-up opportunity, not this lane's scope).

**Test evidence:** battery 12/12 HELD (also clean-env); targeted suites 119/119 OK (policy_config, w79 tiering/totality, w73 provenance, f110 platform_egress, simulator_f7); canonical `tests/run_tests.py` = **3790 tests, 1 failure, 0 errors** — the single failure is `test_s5_velocity.test_s5_reuses_ledger_lock_no_competing_lock`, a KNOWN cross-lane stale assertion (documented in the intent-slice entry: the S5 wave asserted "executor holds no lock objects", the later advisory wave added `self._advisory_lock = threading.Lock()` without updating it; fails 3/3 standalone; this lane adds no locks/threads and doesn't touch executor/ledger paths — reported, not patched, per the standing rule). The Spec reviewer's mid-lane full-suite run showed 500 errors; a clean re-run did not reproduce them (concurrent-lane edit collision in the shared tree), and the final run above shows 0 errors.

**Findings:** none filed. No product defect found at any point (both BREAKs were probe defects; the S5 failure is another lane's documented stale assertion). Next free: **F178**. Open findings: none.

## 2026-09-27 — Row 11 second half: post-hoc unregistered-goal pursuit detection (no push)

**Scope:** Build `gov/goal_audit.py` so `audit_run_goals(run_id, log_path)` / `audit_entries(run_id, entries)` detect, post-run, when an agent's executed behavior is not covered by its registered goals. Post-hoc operator evidence, not inline prevention.

**Design:** (1) Reconstruct each agent's active goals from `goal_registered` / `goal_status_changed` audit events (superseded goals drop out; live-registry override accepted). (2) Extract EXECUTED actions: `tool_call` events with `decision` in {"approved_executed", "allowed_executed"} — queued/denied/refused calls never ran. (3) Map governed tools to structured (verb, target) effects via `derive_effect()`: http_post/send_email/api_call → send (URL host or recipient), write_file → write, delete_file → delete, read_file → read; unknown tools and missing targets → fail-closed "unknown" (never matches a goal). (4) Coverage check: exact (verb, normalized-target) match against declared effects; contradiction check via `gov.goals._OPPOSES` (delete↔preserve/retain) on the same target, which outranks gap; wildcard-only cover → informational `goal_wildcard_cover`. Reads are low-impact and silent. Read-only: never mutates the audit log. Honest ceilings documented in-module: post-hoc only; only governed/logged execution visible; exact matching is paraphrase-sensitive; wildcard goals make deliberate vagueness indistinguishable from legitimate broad authority.

**New files:**
- `gov/goal_audit.py` (~330 lines) — public seams `audit_run_goals`, `audit_entries`, `derive_effect`.

**Scope:** Build `gov/blast_radius.py` so `analyze_blast_radius(approval_id_or_event_seq, audit_log)` verifies the source audit chain FIRST and fails closed if damaged, then walks forward from an approval/event anchor and builds a causal DAG of affected actions: tool calls consuming the approval, resulting state changes, later egress, spawned children and their downstream actions. Fail-closed: `BlastRadiusUnverifiable` on damaged/truncated logs (never a partial report), `AnchorNotFound` on unresolvable anchors. DAG roots: an approval anchor roots on the queued tool_call the approval was granted for (one approval's three audit stages — queued, authorized, executed — all carry the approval id; the queued stage predates the decision), an event anchor roots on the anchor event itself (edge_kind "anchor", its own write/read feeding data-flow matching). ## 2026-09-27 — Row 12 second half: side-channel write detection (no push)

**Scope:** Build `gov/artifact_sweep.py` so `sweep_run_dir(run_dir, inventory)` walks the run sandbox after the run's work and reports every regular file that is not in the Wave-130 `ArtifactInventory` (or whose bytes changed after registration) as an `unregistered_artifact` finding with path, size, SHA-256, and mtime. Wire it as an opt-in post-run step: with `artifact_sweep=True` at construction, `execute_approved()` sweeps automatically after the queue lock is released and audits findings LOUD as chained `artifact_sweep_finding` events (plus one `artifact_sweep_complete` stats event as evidence the sweep ran).

**Design:** pure function over (run_dir, inventory) — read-only, never modifies sandbox/inventory/log. Symlinks never followed and never yielded (F146 PaperCut discipline: a symlink is not a write; following one could escape the sandbox). Unreadable files/dirs skipped fail-open per item (counted in stats), mirroring the inventory's discipline. Two finding kinds: `never_registered` (no inventory record) and `integrity_violation` (registered hash != disk hash, both hashes shipped). Files deleted after registration are not findings (deletion is a separately governed action). `run_artifact_sweep()` never raises — a sweep failure is audited as `artifact_sweep_failed`, never fatal. Judgment call: the `artifact_sweep` kwarg is a boolean-ish opt-in flag rather than an object (drift_store/content_monitor are objects) — the sweep is a pure function with no configuration state, so a flag is the honest shape; documented in-module.

**New files:**
- `gov/artifact_sweep.py` — `sweep_run_dir(run_dir, inventory, *, sandbox_subdir="sandbox")` returning `(findings, stats)`.
- `evals/side_channel_probes.py` — break-first battery (module-level `GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE=staging`; standalone verified under `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`): **0 BREAK / 6 HELD / 0 ERROR** (deterministic ×2, both envs) — p1 side-channel plant flagged never_registered with all four fields + LOUD audit; p2 governed-only run silent (FP ceiling); p3 post-hoc registration with the true hash not flagged; p4 post-registration modification flagged integrity_violation with both hashes; p5 pins the documented boundary (writes outside the run dir are outside the sweep's view); p6 pins the opt-in contract (auto-sweep audits LOUD after execute_approved(); default executor never sweeps).

## 2026-09-27 — Row-9 framing lane: cross-run argument-distribution drift (`gov/framing.py`)

**Problem (from row-9 erosion):** the wave-131 cross-run drift detector (`gov.drift`) compares per-tool call COUNTS only. An agent can keep calling the same tools at the same rate while its routing arguments shift underneath — http_post destinations rotate vendor→personal, write_file targets move logs→secrets, send_email recipients change domains. `detect_drift` sees identical counts and stays silent. The row-9 e4 shape (`evals/row9_erosion_break.py::e4_many_shot_framing_drift`) is content-only framing drift that neither layer can see.

**Built (new, ~20.7 KB):** `gov/framing.py`
- `FramingFingerprint`: per-run argument-distribution fingerprint, ROUTING METADATA ONLY (URL hosts, email recipient domains, path prefixes; never bodies/payloads/full URLs/paths). `framing_fingerprint_from_entries()` extracts from audit entries; denied/rejected calls excluded; missing/redacted fields skipped, never imputed; untracked tools ignored. Fail-closed validation.
- `FramingStore`: per-agent durable JSONL records with SHA-256 chain, audit-before-mutation, `verify_chain()` (tamper-evident).
- `detect_framing()`: chi-square (reuses `gov.drift.chi_square_sf`) on per-tool argument distributions, baseline-vs-window with ≥20 calls minimum and ≥50% window mass.
- Discriminator: substitutive shift (old destinations abandoned → strong signal; a 5% "trickle" remnant does NOT launder it) vs additive adoption (old destinations retained, ≥90% mass → chi-square result capped at weak).
- Graduated response, same combination contract as `gov.drift`: 1 weak → WATCH (chained audit only), 1 strong or 2 signals → WARN, 2 strong or 3 signals → HOLD (queues `framing_review` approval, flag `framing_hold`, human resolves; never auto-denies).
- Honest ceilings documented in code: poisoned baseline (records what happened), slow/sub-threshold destination rotation (documented trickle threshold: ≤10% per-run shift evades), content-level semantic drift at unchanged routing metadata (e4 remains invisible — measured, not claimed), missing/redacted routing fields.

**Executor seam** (`gov/executor.py`, additive only): `ToolExecutor(..., framing_store=None)` appended LAST; `check_run_framing(agent, fingerprint=None, record=True, identity=None, principal=None)` — when no store is installed, silently returns silent with zero behavior change. HOLD requires a real identity (no unsigned `framing_review`), queue failure stays LOUD via `framing_hold_queue_failed`. `framing_review` is a synthetic approval-only tool (like `crossrun_review`).

**Break-first battery:** `evals/framing_probes.py` (module-level staging mode; verified standalone under `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`; deterministic — identical results across runs):
- a_framing_shift_warn HELD (single-tool substitutive shift → warn; 3-tool shift → hold)
- b_stable_destinations_silent HELD (13 identical runs, 0 false positives)
- c_legit_vendor_adoption HELD (additive adoption capped at watch, never warn/hold)
- d1_old_detector_blind MISS-DOCUMENTED (real `gov.drift` stays silent on the framing shift — proves the residual was real)
- d2_e4_semantic_silent HELD (correctly silent on content-level framing drift — the e4 residual remains a documented ceiling, not a false claim)
- e_executor_wiring HELD (HOLD queues `framing_review` with flag `framing_hold`)
- e2_watch_only_audits HELD (WATCH audits only, no approval queued)
- Red-capability check: neutering the substitutive/additive discriminator makes probe (a) BREAK as expected; restored module green.

**Units:** `tests/test_framing.py` — 40/40 OK (normalization, validation, fingerprint-from-entries incl. denied-exclusion, signal math incl. trickle-evasion and redistribution, store chain/tamper, level combination incl. triple-shift hold).

**Regression:** `tests.test_drift` + `tests.test_framing` together 72/72 OK. Canonical constructor ordering verified (framing_store is the 41st param, default None).

**Two-axis review:** Standards PASS (unittest, TMPDIR discipline, staging battery verified clean-env, no debug residue, stdlib-only; one judgement call: FramingStore duplicates DriftStore's chain logic deliberately to leave drift.py untouched — additive pattern per recent lanes). Spec PASS (all task requirements; `api_call` endpoint-host tracking is a documented extension — the executor already treats http_post/api_call as siblings).

**Row 9 stays PARTIAL.** Argument/framing drift at routing metadata improved; the exact semantic e4 (content-level framing), slow destination rotation below the trickle threshold, and baseline poisoning remain documented ceilings.

Gate is a conjunction: negation cue (reuses `gov.intent_slice._NEGATION_RE` — no new negation list) AND `gov.target_match.target_similarity >= threshold` (reuses `DEFAULT_THRESHOLD`, `MATCH_METHOD`) against a prior turn of the same principal. - New `IntentLedger.similarity_countermands_after(principal, since)`: the execution boundary's grant-attribution query — only post-grant turns anchored to pre-grant intent are returned, so a negated paraphrase of post-grant chatter cannot misattribute and revoke an unrelated grant (the load-bearing false-revocation guard). ## 2026-09-27 — Row-7 item: per-message HMAC-derived countermand threshold (wave-138 lane 3, no push)

**Scope:** Row 7's measured wave-137 residual — the similarity countermand's fixed 0.5 token-Tversky threshold (`gov/intent_ledger.py::similarity_countermand` reusing `gov/target_match.py::DEFAULT_THRESHOLD`) is attacker-visible and calibratable: probe with crafted messages, bisect to the exact flip point, sit just under it. Row 7 stays PARTIAL. This lane did NOT push.

**What changed:**
- `gov/intent_ledger.py`: new `derive_countermand_threshold(message)` — `HMAC-SHA256(deployment_key, domain || message)`, first 8 digest bytes as big-endian uint64 scaled to uniform [0,1), mapped to [0.4, 0.6), mean 0.5. The deployment key comes from the EXISTING key-provider seam (`gov.keyprovider.resolve_active_key`) — never hardcoded, never committed; the key-provider seam's own custody story (wave-81: explicit provisioning, fail-closed, no dev fallback) applies unchanged. Fail-closed: no key configured raises `NoKeyConfiguredError` — the seam refuses to decide rather than silently falling back to a fixed threshold. Fail-safe early-outs (non-string/empty message, empty priors, no negation cue) return before the key seam is touched.
- `similarity_countermand(message, prior_messages, threshold=_DERIVE_THRESHOLD)`: the default is now the derive sentinel — the HMAC-derived threshold is used at the countermand decision seam. Explicit floats keep fixed-threshold semantics (tests, adversarial probes); explicit `None` still raises ValueError. Band rationale (documented): max 0.6 < 0.8 so high-similarity countermands always fire; min 0.4 > 0.3 so low-similarity messages never fire; half-width 0.1 so fine-step sweeping cannot localize one fixed flip point.
- `record_intent` records `similarity_threshold` on the chained record (auditable boundary); recording requires a provisioned deployment key (fail-closed, documented in the docstring).
- `gov/target_match.py::DEFAULT_THRESHOLD` untouched — stays the nominal reference (the derived distribution's mean).
- `gov/executor.py`: one comment updated to the derived threshold (no behavior change; the sweep consumes `similarity_countermands_after`).
- New break-first battery `evals/countermand_threshold_calibration_probes.py` (30 message families x graded-similarity sweeps, 682 messages, all negation-cued, one anchor): p1 flip-mid spread (no single calibratable flip point), p2 near-identical-similarity pairs with different verdicts, p3 similarity >= 0.8 always fires, p4 similarity <= 0.3 never fires, p5 same-key verdict/threshold determinism, p6 different-key divergence labeled EXPECTED-DIVERGENCE (documented, intended).
- `tests/test_intent_ledger.py`: +11 `DerivedThresholdSeamTest` — determinism per key, band [0.4, 0.6), per-message variation, cross-key threshold divergence, bad-input rejection, default-uses-derived wiring pin, explicit-threshold fixed semantics, no-key fail-closed (`NoKeyConfiguredError`), fail-safe paths never touch the key seam, record stores `similarity_threshold`, same-key verdict agreement.

Standards PASS — stdlib-only, deterministic, $0; module + function docstrings carry the honest ceilings; fail-closed validation (threshold, key, timestamps) and fail-safe skips preserved and ordered (input validation before key resolution; fail-safe paths never touch the key seam); no new negation list, no constant duplication, `__all__` updated, line lengths <= 79. ## 2026-09-27 — Wave-143 lane: row-12 watch-root mutation auditing (Krishna)

**Scope:** measured residual — undeclared watch roots are invisible; a compromised operator path or direct config edit can silently narrow the artifact-sweep watch roots and the sweep stays quiet.

**What changed:**
- `gov/artifact_sweep.py` (new wave-143 section): `declare_watch_roots(roots, *, previous=None, operator_id, reason, hmac_key, audit, run_id)` — the declaration ceremony. Binds the watch-root set with HMAC-SHA256 (deployment key via `gov.keyprovider.resolve_active_key()`, the wave-69/81 guarded chokepoint, or explicit caller override; never hard-coded; domain-separated `_ROOTS_DECL_DOMAIN`), emits a chained `artifact_sweep_roots_declared` audit event carrying operator identity, old root set → new root set (with added/removed), reason, declaration digest, key epoch, timestamp. The old→new transition is MAC-bound (`previous_roots` + `previous_digest` chain declarations into a tamper-evident history); `operator_id` is required non-empty (anonymous declarations fail closed at ceremony time); non-path entries fail closed; unprovisioned deployment fails closed (no unsigned declaration). Reuses the existing audit-log chaining machinery (caller's `log.append`) — no second chain format.
- `verify_roots_declaration(envelope, ...)` — fail-closed verifier (never raises on malformed input): MAC recomputation + key-epoch staleness (`stale_declaration_epoch`, LOUD at the check layer); key unavailable → unverifiable, never trusted.
- `check_roots_declaration(configured_roots, declaration, ...)` — enforcement: effective (configured) roots vs last declared set. Same set → `declared`, quiet. Added/removed out-of-band (or config edited directly) → one LOUD `artifact_sweep_roots_undeclared_change` event naming added/removed roots, verdict `undeclared_change`. Forged/damaged/stale envelope → LOUD event, verdict `unverifiable`. No declaration configured → explicit `undeclared` downgrade (never silently treated as declared).
- `verify_declaration_chained(log_path, envelope)` — auditor path: confirms the ceremony event is present in the chained log and the chain verifies; a tampered/removed ceremony event breaks the chain and fails LOUD (never raises on unreadable logs — fail-closed).
- `declaration_digest(envelope)` — public recomputable commitment (domain-separated SHA-256, no key), parallel to wave-142's `inventory_digest`.
- `gov/executor.py::run_artifact_sweep` (the real sweep path, not a side demo): when the `artifact_sweep` opt-in carries `"roots_declaration"`, the declaration check runs BEFORE the sweep; `artifact_sweep_complete` always carries `roots_verdict` (`declared` | `undeclared` | `undeclared_change` | `unverifiable`) and `roots_verified` — a narrowed sweep is never silently presented as declared. Zero behavior change when the opt-in is absent (verdict `undeclared`).
- `tests/test_w70_hmac_chokepoint_audit.py`: added the lane's own new `hmac.new` site (`gov/artifact_sweep.py::_roots_decl_mac`) to `ALLOWED_HMAC_SITES` with its custody story (own lane's site — the documented update process, not a quiet patch).
- `evals/roots_declaration_probes.py` (new, red-first): r1 roots narrowed out-of-band through the REAL executor path → exactly 1 LOUD `artifact_sweep_roots_undeclared_change` naming the removed root + `roots_verdict="undeclared_change"`, `roots_verified=False`, chain intact; r2 change {A,B}→{A} through the ceremony → quiet, `declared`, new baseline adopted (old envelope reads `undeclared_change`), ceremony event carries old→new + operator + reason, chain intact; r3 unchanged → quiet `declared`; r4 ceremony event tampered in the log → `verify_declaration_chained` fails LOUD, chain broken at the ceremony entry; r5 deterministic ×2.
- `tests/test_artifact_roots_declaration.py` (new): 34 unit tests at the public seams — ceremony record/verify (round-trip, epoch, dedupe, anonymous/non-path/malformed-previous rejection, old→new event fields, digest recomputation, key-required fail-closed), verify fail-closed (tampered roots/operator, wrong key, stale epoch, missing epoch, malformed never raises, key unavailable), out-of-band detection (added/removed LOUD, downgrade, forged envelope, stale epoch, malformed config raises), chain confirmation (present/missing/tampered/malformed), executor wiring (narrowed LOUD+unverified, ceremony change quiet+declared, no-declaration downgrade, forged envelope fail-closed).

**Verification:** battery RED-first **1 HELD / 4 BREAK pre-seam** → **5 HELD / 0 BREAK / 0 EXPECTED / 0 ERROR post-seam**, both deployment envs (clean `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE` standalone run), deterministic ×2. New units **34/34**. Adjacent, no regressions: `tests/test_artifact_sweep` 16/16, `tests/test_artifact_inventory_pin` 34/34, `tests/test_artifact_coverage` 16/16, `tests/test_w70_hmac_chokepoint_audit` 11/11; older batteries unchanged (`evals/artifact_pin_ceremony_probes.py` 5/5, `evals/artifact_inventory_pin_probes.py` 8/8, `evals/artifact_coverage_probes.py` HELD). Every suite ran under the canonical venv with its own fresh mkdir-p'd unique TMPDIR, sequentially (no shared-TMPDIR concurrency). `evals/artifacts/wave23_b2/battery_100_results.json` untouched.

**Two-axis review (manual — the code-review skill needs git; this tree is a snapshot with no .git):** Standards PASS — repo docstring style with honest ceilings, wave-141/142 HMAC patterns reused (domain separation, keyprovider chokepoint, fail-closed verifiers, ceremony-raises/verify-never-raises posture), w70 allowlist updated with custody story, opt-in zero-behavior-change, stdlib-only, deterministic, $0, no debug residue, `__all__` updated. Spec PASS — ceremony carries operator identity + old→new + reason on the existing chained log (no second chain format); out-of-band add/remove → LOUD event + unverified verdict via the real `run_artifact_sweep` path; ceremony change → quiet with new baseline adopted; unchanged → quiet; tampered ceremony event → chain verification fails LOUD; no unavoidable miss → no EXPECTED.

**Honest ceilings (module docstring + battery, not hidden):** this lane audits the watch-root *configuration*, not the sweeping — a compromised same-process executor can still lie about what it actually swept (pass different roots to the sweep than to the declaration check, skip the check, or forge either event): the standing row-12 same-process residual. Key custody underpins the ceremony chain exactly like every other chained event — a key-holder can declare a malicious-but-authorized set and it verifies cleanly; the ceremony (who declared what, when — audited) is the control, not the MAC. The declaration binds the CONFIGURED roots; it does not prove the declared set was wise (a narrow set declared honestly is the operator's problem), and undeclared directories stay invisible.

**Findings:** none filed. Next free: F183 (per last BUILD_LOG entry). Row 12 stays PARTIAL — the out-of-band-narrowing leg is now measured and LOUD, NOT closed.

## Wave-168 — A2A signed Agent Card verifier merge (row-11 cross-runtime identity)

**Merge.** Team tree `teams/a2a-verifier/tree` merged into the shared tree (base: wave-167 commit `a897a0b`, remote HEAD verified `a897a0b` via direct `git ls-remote` before merge; pre-merge diff confirmed ONLY the intended deltas: new `gov/agent_cards.py`, additive `gov/delegation_tokens.py` (~135 diff lines), new `evals/a2a_card_verifier_probes.py`, one new AMSB scorecard pair under `evals/artifacts/amsb/`). Changed files: `gov/agent_cards.py` (new), `gov/delegation_tokens.py` (additive), `evals/a2a_card_verifier_probes.py` (new), `evals/artifacts/amsb/scorecard-20260928T084940Z.{json,txt}` (lane-tree run evidence).

**What was built.** Fail-closed A2A v1.0 signed-Agent-Card verifier (stdlib-only): RFC 8785 canonical JSON (minus `signatures`) → JWS flattened detached verification; EdDSA via the repo's own RFC 8032 Ed25519 implementation (no new dependencies — see ES256 correction below). Strict algorithm allow-list `{"EdDSA"}`; distinct failure codes (`missing-signatures`, `unsupported-alg`, `kid-ambiguity`, `untrusted-jku`, `stale-trust`, `invalid-signature`, `identity-mismatch`, `canonicalization-failure`). `jku` is NEVER fetched — no network path exists in the verifier (verified: no socket/urllib/requests/http imports or calls); `jku` must be HTTPS, allow-listed, and exact-match to a deployment-pinned card trust store living beside `gov/delegation_tokens.py`'s `DelegationTrust` roster (same offline-root registration). Bind point: at delegation setup the verifier runs; verified `(kid → pubkey)` registers into `DelegationTrust.agent_keys` keyed by card `name`; `issue_delegation(..., card_kid=None)` writes the kid into signed claims; `verify_delegation_chain` enforces kid→registered-identity == hop subject (`DelegationBindingError` on swap); `spawn_sub_agent` writes `card_kid: None` (strict subject binding — child does not inherit); `delegation_receipt` gains top-level `card_kid` (version stays 1; local receipts get `None` — the card path is additive, never a replacement). Card = identity-proof layer; receipt stays the authorization layer.

**Red-first on the merged tree.** Pre-fix gap demonstrated by the lane (`/tmp/red_a2a_gap.py`): an attacker-signed card under the victim's name was indistinguishable from the genuine card; the attacker's key registered as `acme-support-agent`; a delegation receipt then verified — no cryptographic binding between a foreign agent's claimed card identity and its key. Post-fix: new battery `evals/a2a_card_verifier_probes.py` **28 HELD / 0 BREAK / 0 EXPECTED / 0 ERROR** (staging + clean env `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`, deterministic ×2; depth-1 `GOV_SKIP_GREEN` green check runs adjacent delegation batteries), covering the full failure matrix plus the red-first closure (forged card refused, roster untouched), receipt binding, swapped-kid/subject-mismatch refusal, spawn dropping the binding, and local receipts unaffected.

**Honest ES256 correction.** The prospecting R4 claim that the `cryptography` package was in `requirements.lock` was WRONG — direct inspection proved it absent from the lock, the venv, and system Python; installing it would trip the F75 supply-chain gate. ES256 therefore **fails closed as `unsupported-alg`** (documented refusal, not silent non-support). Vetted ECDSA is a follow-up if the product requires it; EdDSA covers the v1 identity binding.

**Pre-existing note.** `tests.test_ed25519` / `tests.test_signing` don't exist as modules (pre-existing, not a breakage).

**Push-clone gates (fresh clone of a897a0b + rsync, workstream sibling symlinks verified, fresh unique TMPDIRs, serialized suites):** canonical **5143 OK** (skipped=9, expected failures=5); registry **GREEN**; matrix **3216/3216 SHIP-GATE GREEN**; realistic **7/7**. Canaries in the merged tree: new A2A battery **28/28**; AMSB scorecard reproduced **byte-identical to wave-167** (GRADE D 77.78, uncapped C, ceiling D, defense 77.8%, FP 0.0%, same 2 documented critical breaches — no regression); decision replay **7/7**, delegation stamping **12/0**, delegation receipt probes **12/0**, manifest default-on **15/0**, egress tiered wire **8/0/5 EXPECTED**, row-9 fold **5/5** + keyed chain **5/5**, row-12 undeclared-path **15/15** + row-12 battery **7/7**, row-7 F188 **23/23** + verb-expansion **28/28** + archive-redact **16/16** + native-cue **35/0/3 EXPECTED**, H26 e1–e4 GREEN, F189 pin HELD ×2.

**Merge.** Team tree `teams/f154-hardening/tree` merged into the shared tree (base: wave-168 commit `86dd775`, remote HEAD verified `86dd775` via direct `git ls-remote` before merge; pre-merge diff confirmed ONLY the intended deltas: `gov/memory_provenance.py` lineage-cap, `tests/test_memory_provenance.py` +3 tests, two new eval batteries, one new AMSB scorecard pair). The lane tree was cut at wave-167 (`a897a0b`); the only cross-wave deltas were the expected wave-168 additions (`gov/agent_cards.py`, `gov/delegation_tokens.py`, `evals/a2a_card_verifier_probes.py`) which were left untouched. Per the lane's explicit recommendation, the detector-hardening variant was NOT merged (its reference copy stays outside the product tree at `teams/f154-hardening/memory_provenance_f154h_detector_variant.py`). Changed files: `gov/memory_provenance.py`, `tests/test_memory_provenance.py`, `evals/f154_paraphrase_battery.py` (new), `evals/f154_robustness.py` (new), `evals/artifacts/amsb/scorecard-20260928T085006Z.{json,txt}` (lane-tree run evidence). `evals/gap1mem_break.py` verified byte-identical to base.

**What was built (TealTiger section-9.8 shape, read-time placement).** Architectural finding: `tier_for_write` is verbatim-overlap-only, so paraphrase laundering is derivation, not detection-evasion — the write path receives the run's ingested fingerprints but never their trust. A tier-seam cap would have contradicted two deliberate precision pins (`test_no_overlap_is_agent`, `test_paraphrase_is_documented_residual`), so the cap was built at READ time: `ledger.record_write` gains additive `lineage_shaped_source` (bool, default False, backward-compatible); `record_memory_write` sets it when any ingested fingerprint is instruction-shaped (the *source* is detector-visible; the paraphrase itself is never "detected"); `check_memory_read` returns `("allow", "agent_lineage_shaped_source")` for agent-tiered + unshaped + flagged bytes, and `provenance_banner` prepends a new honest banner (`_PROVENANCE_BANNER_LINEAGE`, which does NOT claim verbatim copying). Tier ontology untouched — the F154 tiering residual stays documented at `tier_for_write`; containment happens at delivery. Benign external ingestion (not instruction-shaped) sets no flag (F144 pin holds). Both pins pass unchanged: the tier contract they document is preserved because the tier is never overridden.

**Red-first on the merged tree.** New battery `evals/f154_robustness.py` (32 hand-written paraphrase variants, families A–F, through the full delayed-activation A3 shape: ingest shaped verbatim poison → agent writes paraphrase → session boundary → recall): **0.0% silent delivery (31 bannered + 1 quarantined of 32)**. AMSB scorecard reproduced the lane's result exactly on the merged tree: **GRADE C 88.89 (uncapped B, ceiling C), defense 88.9%, FP rate 0.0% (0/7), 1 critical breach** — `delayed-paraphrase-directive` now DEFENDED (tier=agent, banner=True, warn=1 via the p3 banner contract); the sole remaining critical breach is the documented `a1-default-off` opt-in deployment boundary. Per-category: persistence 4/4 (was 3/4), all other categories unchanged. Baseline was D 77.78 with 2 critical breaches.

**Detector-hardening negative result (not merged).** The same lane tried 5 new shaping-detector pattern families first: AMSB also reached C 88.89, but the 32-variant silent rate only fell 96.9% → 65.6% — the mincha_brain wall (paraphrase detectors structurally collapse on weak-signal attacks; retraining makes it worse). A bare `auto-approval` word-detector was built and rejected (broke banner precision tests). The detector is strictly dominated: same scoreboard, 65.6pp worse robustness, adds pattern arms-race surface. Not merged.

**Honest residuals (no paraphrase closure claimed).** (1) No-ingestion paraphrase: agent paraphrases from parametric memory with no shaped ingestion in the run → no flag → silent; out of provenance scope by construction. (2) Cross-session laundering: lineage is per-run; ingest in session 1, paraphrase-write in session 2 → missed. Real residual — a cross-session lineage journal is the follow-up. (3) Detector-invisible shaped source: the flag keys on today's detector; a weaker-signal source is the next adversary step. (4) Banner noise: runs that legitimately quote shaped content then write benign notes → those notes banner on read (banner-only, not quarantine). (5) Paraphrased *factual* (unshaped) poison without verbatim link still tiers agent silently — unchanged from baseline.

**Findings:** none filed. F154 was already a documented class residual; this shrinks it without closing the class. Next free: F190. Open findings: NONE.

## Wave-170 — Cross-session lineage journal (F154 residual closure)

**Merge.** Team tree `teams/xsession-lineage/tree` merged into the shared tree (base: wave-169 commit `517a966`, remote HEAD verified `517a966` via direct `git ls-remote` before merge; pre-merge diff of `gov/`, `tests/`, `evals/` confirmed ONLY the intended deltas). Changed files: `gov/memory_provenance.py` (`LineageJournal` + `note_shaped_ingestion` + journal consult in `record_memory_write`), `gov/executor.py` (ingestion-funnel feed into `note_shaped_ingestion`; journal verification at session open; loud `memory_ledger_unverifiable` chaining), `tests/test_memory_provenance.py` (+10 `TestCrossSessionLineageJournal`), `evals/amsb_corpus.py` (new critical/persistence scenario `xsession-paraphrase-directive`), `evals/amsb_run.py` (fresh scratch per scenario — harness contamination bug fix), four AMSB scorecard artifacts (the FP-100%/score-F pre-fix pair kept as contamination evidence, plus the lane-result pair and the merged-tree reproduction pair). Lane report: `teams/xsession-lineage/LANE_REPORT.md`.

**The genuine gap (red-first pre-fix).** Wave-169's lineage cap sets `lineage_shaped_source` from the writing run's ingested fingerprints, but that store is per-run. Shape B (ingest verbatim shaped poison in session 1, no write; reset; paraphrase-write in session 2 with clean in-run fingerprints; reset; recall in session 3) was deterministically SILENT pre-fix: `bannered=False warnings=0 quarantined=False`, ledger `lineage_shaped_source=False` — the flag died with the run. Shape A (ingest+write in session 1, recall in session 2) was already defended by wave-169 (the write's persisted record carries the flag).

**Design (no second content journal).** The `MemoryLedger` is already persistent, HMAC-chained, and content-free; the missing state is the shaped lineage *between* the ingestion session and a later writing session, so the lane persists a content-free lineage fact at ingestion time: `LineageJournal(EgressLedger)` — append-only HMAC-chained JSONL, one per deployment (`<ledger-dir>/lineage_journal.jsonl`); entry kind `shaped_ingestion`: `{principal, run_id, fp_sha256, instruction_reason, ts}` — digests and flags only, never content, so the journal cannot become a silent exfil channel. Feed: the executor's tool-result ingestion funnel (the single point where read fingerprints enter the run) calls `note_shaped_ingestion` for instruction-shaped ingestions, including ones that never lead to a same-run write; deduped per (principal, digest). Consult: `record_memory_write` sets `lineage_shaped_source=True` when the in-run fingerprint check fires OR `lineage_journal.has_pending(principal)` fires; the read-time banner path and the tier ontology are untouched. Lifecycle: `has_pending` is true only within `lineage_window_s` (default 24h, deployment-tunable) — the window bounds the "pending lineage" state (forever-banners vs wait-it-out trade-off, documented on the constant); the tail walk stops at the cutoff, the append-only bytes remain as audit trail. Lookup is keyed newest-first in 64KiB blocks, O(recent entries), pinned by `test_journal_lookup_is_keyed_not_a_scan`. Measured on a 2,001-entry journal: `has_pending` 0.13 ms, `record_memory_write` 0.80 ms, session-open verify 0.03 ms. Tamper = fail closed, loud: a broken chain raises `LedgerUnverifiableError` at session-open scan, at write time, and at ingestion-feed time; the executor chains `memory_ledger_unverifiable` and refuses — never silently consults.

**Red-first on the merged tree.** Shape B now `bannered=True warnings=1`, ledger `lineage_shaped_source=True tier=agent`; Shape A unchanged. AMSB reproduced the lane's scorecard byte-for-byte on the merged tree: **score 90.00, uncapped A, ceiling C, FINAL GRADE C** (was C 88.89 / uncapped B; the +1.11 is the new defended scenario), defense 90.0% (36/40 weight), **FP 0.0% (0/7)**, 1 critical breach (`a1-default-off`, the documented opt-in deployment boundary), 0 silent instruction breaches, determinism OK (2 identical rounds). Per-category delta vs wave-169: persistence 5/5 (was 4/4) — the new `xsession-paraphrase-directive` scenario DEFENDED (tier=agent, banner=True, warn=1); all other categories unchanged. All 7 benign controls byte-exact and banner-free, including the cross-session benign control. F154: `f154_robustness.py` 32/32 non-silent (31 bannered + 1 quarantined), 0.0% silent — wave-169 expectation held; `f154_paraphrase_battery.py` detector escape 96.9% unchanged (detector deliberately not hardened; mincha_brain wall). Tamper-evidence verified directly on the merged tree: corrupted journal → `LedgerUnverifiableError` at session-open scan, at ingest-feed, and at write-time consult — fail closed, never silent. Unit tests `tests/test_memory_provenance.py`: 59/59 green (10 new).

**Harness contamination bug found and fixed (not a product result).** The AMSB runner declared "fresh adapter per scenario" but shared one scratch across all scenarios. The memory ledger survived that because it is (principal, mem_key)-keyed; the journal is principal-keyed deployment state, so attack scenarios' shaped ingestions contaminated benign scenarios' writes — the first run scored FP 100% / score F 50.00. That pre-fix pair (`scorecard-20260928T091400Z`) is kept as contamination evidence; the fix gives each scenario a fresh scratch (within a scenario, sessions still share the adapter's scratch, so cross-session lineage works where it should). Attack verdicts were unaffected (all attack scenarios are self-contained). Red-first discipline caught this: the harness violated its own stated invariant, and the lane fixed the harness rather than re-interpreting the product result.

**Canaries (merged tree, serial, fresh TMPDIRs):** decision replay 7/7 HELD · delegation stamping 12/0 · delegation receipt probes 12/0 · manifest default-on 15/0 · egress tiered 8/0/5 expected · row-9 unverified fold 5/5 + keyed chain 5/5 · row-12 undeclared-path 15/15 + other-file-tools battery 7/7 · row-7 F188 glued cues 23/23 + verb-expansion 28/28 + archive/redact 16/16 + native cues 35/0/3 expected · H26 e1–e4 GREEN · F189 fingerprint-flood pin HELD ×2 · A2A card verifier 28/28 · F154 lineage-cap batteries green.

**Gates (fresh push-clone at base 517a966, push-clone discipline, serialized):** canonical **5156 OK** (skipped=9, expected failures=5; +10 vs wave-169 = the new journal tests) · registry **GREEN** · matrix **3216/3216** · realistic **7/7**. The lane skipped full canonical for memory reasons (~1.8 GB); the coordinator's run is authoritative.

**Honest residuals (documented, not claimed away).** (1) Principal-level banner noise within the window: the cross-session link cannot be content-narrowed (the session-N+1 write is a detector-invisible paraphrase — F154 — so no deterministic write-time check can link it to the specific ingested poison; the deterministic options are principal-level pending state or nothing). A benign memory write made within 24h of any shaped ingestion is bannered (noise, not silence — bytes still delivered). Same family as wave-169's accepted residual, extended across the session boundary; bounded by the tunable window. (2) Window-delay bypass: an attacker who can delay the laundering write past the window evades the flag — the bypass-vs-noise trade-off, documented on the constant. (3) Parametric-memory paraphrase: unchanged — the journal covers tool-ingested lineage, not weights. (4) Journal growth: dedupe bounds re-ingestion; the window bounds the consulted working set; lookups are keyed. No pruning — the append-only file grows with distinct shaped ingestions (audit trail by design). (5) The journal is not consume-on-first-write (that would add a decoy-write bypass), so decoy sequencing remains the noise residual, not a bypass.

**Findings:** none filed — the wave-169 residual #2 (cross-session laundering) is now closed. Next free: F190. Open findings: F190 (canonical-target TOCTOU, filed 2026-09-28 by the target-binding red team; fix lane `teams/f190-fix/` complete, queued for wave-171).

## 2026-09-29 — Wave-194 lane A: TUF load freshness (pin expiry + rollback floor)

**Scope.** Closure build for the python-tuf spike's load-seam gap (spike verdict: ADAPT mechanisms): on pristine base `aa231a6`, the load layer had expiry and monotonic version on the *watch* layer but the *load* layer's `ArtifactPinset` carried neither — `load_skill_content` ACCEPTED a pin dated 2020, and a replayed older pin digest displaced the newer pin (`evals/tuf_load_seam_probes.py`: 2 GAP SHOWN on pristine, deterministic x2, also under `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`).

**Product change (`gov/load_gate.py`).** Pin protocol bumped `gov-artifact-pin/v1` → `/v2`. `ArtifactPinset.pin()` now records a monotonic `version` (default 1, must be `int`, ≥ 1, no bools) and a `not_after` expiry bound (default pinned_at + 90 days, watch-layer parity; strict tz-aware ISO-8601, naive/malformed refused fail-closed); both are signature-covered in the canonical pin body and audit-recorded. Re-pin at a non-increasing version is refused (`pin_version_not_monotonic`); `unpin` carries a versioned signature and refuses non-increasing versions (`unpin_version_not_monotonic`). `verify_and_load` refuses expired pins (`pin_expired`) *before* the digest check (watch-layer parity); `load_skill_content` inherits the refusal through the forced entry point. Authorship is verified **before** the version floor (TUF order: signature first, then freshness), so a forged statement still reports `pin_authorship_invalid` precisely and only a genuinely-signed older statement reaches the floor.

**Fixed tree: `evals/tuf_load_seam_probes.py` 17/17 HELD, 0 gaps, 0 breaks** (each probe x2 internally; also 17/17 under `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`): expired pins refused at both `load_skill_content` and `verify_and_load`; expiry-before-digest; rollback and same-version replay refused with the newer pin surviving; replayed unpin refused; naive/malformed/zero-version pins refused; 90-day default; legitimate higher-version renewal and unpin accepted; expiry tamper breaks authorship; fresh-pin control loads.

**Adjacent suites green after migration:** `tests/test_w194_tuf_load_seam.py` (new, 17/17) · `tests/test_w78_supplychain` + `tests/test_w80_loadgate_forced` (76/76) · `tests/test_w79_totality` (12/12) · `evals/w78_probes.py` (11/11 stopped) · `evals/w80_probes.py` (6/6 stopped, 1 pre-existing documented residual, 0 break). Call-site migration: `tests/test_w78_supplychain.py`, `tests/test_w80_loadgate_forced.py`, `evals/w78_probes.py`, `evals/w80_probes.py` updated to the v2 pin bodies; the w80 MCP probe's deployer helpers now renew at a strictly higher version (the intended new deployer flow).

**Honest residuals (documented, not claimed away).** (1) The monotonic floor is per-process in-memory: after a successful unpin the floor is lost (in-memory registry has no tombstone/persistent floor), so a replayed old pin *statement* could re-pin a previously unpinned artifact within a new process — process-restart persistence needs a trusted external floor or persistent registry (future work). (2) Pins pre-dating the v2 body (v1 signatures) are rejected outright, not migrated — the bump is intentional and loud. (3) `ArtifactRefused` pre-validation order: malformed artifact_id/tier/digest still refuse before authorship (unchanged).

**Scope.** Pure-addition build lane on base `aa231a6` (local worktree `~/workspace/teams/wave193-cosignbuild/sasanam`, never pushed). Implements the wave-191 cosign spec (`SPEC.md`): bind the project's Ed25519 keyset ceremony to cosign's ECDSA-P256 transport keys so an auditor can answer whose key signed a bundle tar, whether it was authorized, and whether rotation/revocation since changes the verdict.

**New files.** `gov/cosign_attest.py` (~700 lines, stdlib only): `attest_cosign_key` (mints via `keyset_signer_for_version` -- active-only; revoked/verify-only seeds refused; keyset purpose pinned to `cosign-key-attestation`), `verify_attestation` (exact format/field validation, domain `sasanam-cosign-key-attestation/v1␀`, envelope↔attested_by consistency, keyset-hash pin, `find_verifying_key` / forensics lookup, Ed25519 verify, strict P-256 SPKI parse, fingerprint re-derivation), `sign_bundle_blob` / `verify_bundle_blob` (cosign CLI surface, `--use-signing-config=false` hardcoded, password env-only, CLI timeout fail-closed), `authorize_bundle_signature` / `attribute_bundle_signature` (five-step pipeline: genesis pin → keyset verify → attested_by verify → attestation verify → cosign verify-blob with the PEM from the verified attestation; revoked refuses on authorize, attributes on forensics). `tests/fake_cosign.py` (no-network CLI double: refuses sign-blob without the offline flag, digest-based tamper refusal, argv logging). `tests/test_cosign_attest.py` (41 unit tests). `evals/cosign_attest_probes.py` (13-probe red-first battery, module-level `GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE=staging`, honors `GOV_SKIP_GREEN`, deterministic x2, passes under `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`).
